In their own words

“We have a small problem.”

The calmest voices in the worst moments: what pilots and passengers actually said when everything went wrong. Every quote comes from a cockpit or radio recording, or was said on the record, and is checked against at least three independent sources, linked under it.

  • Ladies and gentlemen, this is your captain speaking. We have a small problem. All four engines have stopped. We are doing our damnedest to get them under control. I trust you are not in too much distress.

    Eric MoodyBritish Airways Flight 9 · 24 June 1982

    Said to: Passengers, over the cabin speakers

    British Airways Flight 9 had flown into an unseen cloud of volcanic ash over Indonesia at night, and one by one all four engines of the Boeing 747 flamed out. Captain Moody calmly told the passengers what had happened while the crew kept trying to relight them. The jumbo glided down for several minutes before the engines came back, and it landed safely in Jakarta with all 263 people aboard unhurt.

    Photo: G B_NZ · CC BY-SA 2.0

    Sources: 1 2 3 4Read the story →

  • We're gonna be in the Hudson.

    Chesley "Sully" SullenbergerUS Airways Flight 1549 · 15 January 2009

    Said to: Air traffic control

    Geese had knocked out both engines of US Airways Flight 1549 minutes after take-off from LaGuardia. Controllers offered runways at LaGuardia and Teterboro, but Sullenberger judged the Airbus could reach neither and told them where he was going instead. All 155 people aboard survived the landing on the river.

    Photo: United States Department of State · Public domain

    Sources: 1 2 3Read the story →

  • This is the captain. Brace for impact.

    Chesley "Sully" SullenbergerUS Airways Flight 1549 · 15 January 2009

    Said to: Passengers, over the cabin speakers

    With no time to explain more, this was the only announcement Sullenberger made before the ditching. The flight attendants then shouted their own brace commands at the passengers until the plane hit the water.

    Photo: United States Department of State · Public domain

    Sources: 1 2 3 4Read the story →

  • For 42 years, I've been making small, regular deposits in this bank of experience, education and training. And on January 15, the balance was sufficient so that I could make a very large withdrawal.

    Chesley "Sully" SullenbergerUS Airways Flight 1549 · February 2009

    Said to: Katie Couric, CBS News

    Asked how he had pulled off the landing, Sullenberger put it down to decades of practice rather than luck or heroism.

    Outlets printed the end slightly differently, as "a very large withdrawal" or "a sudden, large withdrawal".

    Photo: United States Department of State · Public domain

    Sources: 1 2 3Read the story →

  • No, it's not on fire, but part of it's missing.

    Tammie Jo ShultsSouthwest Airlines Flight 1380 · 17 April 2018

    Said to: Philadelphia air traffic control

    An engine on Southwest Flight 1380 had come apart over Pennsylvania, and debris broke a window. When a controller asked whether the Boeing 737 was on fire, Shults answered in an even voice, then added that passengers said there was a hole and someone had gone out. She landed the damaged plane in Philadelphia.

    Photo: Thomas P. Milne, US Navy · Public domain

    Sources: 1 2 3Read the story →

  • You want to be particular and make it a runway, huh?

    Al HaynesUnited Airlines Flight 232 · 19 July 1989

    Said to: Sioux City approach control

    United Flight 232 had lost all its hydraulics and could only be steered by changing the power of its two remaining engines. When the controller cleared it to land on any runway, Haynes joked back, and the crew laughed in the middle of the emergency. 184 of the 296 people aboard survived the crash landing.

    A transcript Haynes later used in his talks has "You don't want to be particular…"

    Photo: Wayne Russell · Public domain

    Sources: 1 2 3Read the story →

  • Are you guys ready? Okay. Let's roll.

    Todd BeamerUnited Airlines Flight 93 · 11 September 2001

    Said to: Fellow passengers, overheard on an Airfone call

    Beamer had been on the seat-back phone with GTE supervisor Lisa Jefferson, telling her the passengers planned to rush the hijackers. These were the last words she heard before the line went quiet. The revolt stopped the hijackers reaching their target, and the plane came down in a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania.

    Photo: MysidOriginal by the 9/11 commission · Public domain

    Sources: 1 2 3Read the story →

  • I did what I had to do. I saved the plane, the passengers, the crew. I think that was the only decision. I don't think I'm a hero.

    Damir YusupovUral Airlines Flight 178 · 16 August 2019

    Said to: Reporters in Yekaterinburg

    A day after a flock of gulls disabled both engines of Ural Airlines Flight 178, Yusupov had landed the Airbus A321 with its wheels up in a cornfield outside Moscow. All 233 aboard lived, and the same day he was made a Hero of Russia, though he told reporters he did not see himself that way.

    Translated from Russian, so the wording differs a little between outlets.

    Photo: Presidential Press Service of Russia · CC BY 4.0

    Sources: 1 2 3Read the story →
